title: F# Quick Reference
description: Look up a lesson idea, see its small example, and check a common mistake. Open the linked lesson for setup and practice steps.

entries.name: Print a greeting
entries.summary: printfn prints formatted output and a new line. %s stands for text.
notes: Match the format marker to the value type.

entries.name: Keep a named value
entries.summary: let gives a name to a value. It cannot be changed unless declared mutable.
notes: Use parentheses to group a calculation passed to printfn.

entries.name: Name a calculation
entries.summary: A function is defined with let and an input name. Its expression is the result.
notes: F# function inputs follow the function name with spaces.

entries.name: Choose a value
entries.summary: if is an expression with then and else results.

example.code:
let score = 8
let message = if score >= 5 then "Pass" else "Try again"
printfn "%s" message

notes: The two result branches must agree in type.

entries.name: Keep a list
entries.summary: List items are separated by semicolons. List.head reads the first item.
notes: List.head fails on an empty list; tryHead returns an option.

entries.name: Transform each value
entries.summary: List.map applies a function to every item and returns a new list.

example.code:
let values = [2; 3] |> List.map (fun n -> n * 2)
printfn "%A" values

notes: The pipe sends the list into the next function call.

entries.name: Keep matching values
entries.summary: List.filter keeps values that pass a Boolean test.

example.code:
let values = [4; 8; 9] |> List.filter (fun n -> n >= 7)
printfn "%A" values

notes: The test must return true or false.

entries.name: Unpack a pair
entries.summary: A tuple groups values. Pattern matching can give names to its parts.
notes: Match the same number of tuple positions.

entries.name: Group named fields
entries.summary: A record has named fields. A new record can copy an old one with one field changed.
notes: The with expression creates a new value.

entries.name: Handle an absent value
entries.summary: An option is Some(value) or None. Pattern matching handles both.

example.code:
let score: int option = None
let value = match score with | Some n -> n | None -> 0
printfn "%d" value

notes: Handle None instead of assuming a value exists.

entries.name: Name a set of cases
entries.summary: A union describes a fixed set of cases. match selects an action for a case.

example.code:
type Light = Red | Green
let light = Green
let message = match light with | Red -> "Stop" | Green -> "Go"
printfn "%s" message

notes: Cover every union case in a match.

entries.name: Combine list values
entries.summary: List.fold carries a result through the list. The starting total is zero here.

example.code:
let total = [2; 3; 4] |> List.fold (fun sum n -> sum + n) 0
printfn "%d" total

notes: The starting value affects the result.
